Assist with recruitment, induction, training, and competency assessments for new and existing team members. Support the completion of probation reviews, one-to-one meetings, appraisals, and development plans. Monitor staff attendance, punctuality, and compliance with departmental procedures, escalating concerns where appropriate. title: Medical Receptionist
description: We are looking for an enthusiastic and hard working Medical Receptionists to join our friendly team based across our two sites at the heart of Redhill and in Merstham. We have a part time position working Monday-Friday. This will be a combination of shifts either morning from 8:00-13.00 or afternoon from 13:00-19:00. Previous experience of working in a similar environment would be desirable although fast learners with an ability to excel in a faced-past, ever evolving industry would be ideal candidates. The main responsibilities of this role include dealing with patient enquiries face to face, over the telephone and through our interactive website. A high level of customer service skills are required and as well as clear communication with GPs and other healthcare professionals to ensure that a safe and efficient service is provided to our patient population is vital. Daily administrative tasks will include booking appointments, prescription management, registering new patients, managing emails and and internal electronic tasks via our clinical system. Managing appointment requests and queries via our interactive website is a key part of this role as this is the main route of communication between patients and the practice. Opening and closing the surgery in line with our security protocols and maintaining oversight of the waiting room are other key responsibilities. EMIS Web is our clinical I.T system and Accurx is used as our digital messaging platform. Full training will be provided as part of the induction process. Job Purpose As part of a team, to achieve a smooth running and efficient surgery for both GPs and patients and to provide all necessary administrative support required by the Practice Prime Objectives To provide an efficient and professional reception service during surgeries and clinics To ensure that all record keeping, both manual and computerised, is accurate and up to date To respect patient confidentiality at all times Main Duties Running the appointment and associated IT systems accurately and to maximise use of available time Repeat prescribing as directed by the doctors Dealing with queries by reference to both computerised and manual records Clerical work related to the reception function Opening and closing premises, ensuring readiness for use and security out of hours Other such duties as required for the smooth running of the practice

title: Senior Receptionist/Administrator (Patient Services Team)
description: We are a forward thinking, busy and friendly General Practice based in Guildford, looking to recruit an enthusiastic person to join our Patient Services Team in a Senior role. Merrow Park Surgery provides care for 12,000 patients in its surrounding areas. We are seeking an enthusiastic, organised and motivated Senior Receptionist/Administrator to join our friendly and supportive Patient Services Team . This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced primary care receptionist/administrator who is looking to take the next step in their career and take on a senior role within a busy GP practice. The successful candidate will play a key part in supporting the day-to-day running of our front-line patient services, helping to ensure that patients receive an efficient, professional and compassionate service. Key Responsibilities Supporting and supervising members of the Patient Services Team. Providing a high standard of customer service to patients, colleagues and external stakeholders. Managing reception and administrative processes efficiently and accurately. Processing and managing patient requests through the Practice's Total Triage system. Opening and closing the practice in accordance with established procedures. Scanning, coding and processing clinical correspondence and patient records accurately and in a timely manner. Maintaining the integrity and accuracy of electronic patient records. Liaising with patients, GPs, healthcare professionals and external agencies. Assisting with staff training, workflow management and service improvement initiatives. Supporting the Practice Management Team with operational and administrative tasks as required. Care Navigation Oversee and coordinate the care navigation processes within the PST team to ensure all patient requests are triaged and directed appropriately according to clinical protocols and practice procedures. Provide support and training to new staff in effective care navigation and triage processes. Liaise directly with duty doctors to manage complex or urgent cases, ensuring patients are signposted correctly and efficiently. Monitor care navigation outcomes to identify areas for improvement and implement service changes where required. Act as a point of escalation for reception staff dealing with difficult or uncertain care navigation scenarios. Administration Ensure all administrative protocols and procedures are followed by the reception team, providing guidance where needed. Act as a senior point of contact for complex patient enquiries or complaints, resolving issues with professionalism and sensitivity. Monitor the quality and accuracy of patient record-keeping, ensuring compliance with data protection and confidentiality standards. Oversee new patient registrations, de-registrations, and record updates, ensuring accuracy and consistency. Supervise the processing of appointments, tasks, and email communication within the team, ensuring timeliness and attention to detail. Coordinate cover for clinics such as menopause, dermatology, and minor ops in the absence of colleagues. Delegate administrative tasks to team members while maintaining overall responsibility for their timely and correct completion. Maintain oversight of the practice website content in coordination with the management team, ensuring information is up to date and accessible. Premises Management Assist with the opening and securing of the premises, ensuring staff are aware of the correct procedures and are trained accordingly. Be a point of contact for premises-related issues and liaise with external contractors when necessary. Conduct regular checks to ensure consulting rooms and communal areas are clean, safe, and adequately stocked for clinical use. Report and monitor all Health and Safety concerns, escalating where appropriate and ensuring corrective actions are taken. Maintain oversight of the reception area to ensure it remains welcoming, orderly, and compliant with health and safety regulations. Training and Development Support the training and induction of new reception staff, providing mentoring and coaching as required. Identify development needs within the team and work with management to arrange appropriate training or support. Lead by example in attending and contributing to team meetings, PLT sessions, and other development opportunities. Ensure all team members are compliant with mandatory training and assist in tracking their training records. Keep own knowledge and skills up to date, particularly in regard to care navigation, clinical systems, and NHS processes. General Responsibilities Act as deputy to the Assistant Practice Manager as required. Assist in the implementation of new systems, processes, or software and support team members during transition periods. Attend management meetings when requested to provide updates and feedback from the reception team. Promote a positive and professional working environment, encouraging teamwork and a patient-centred approach in all duties. Uphold and model the practices values, policies, and commitment to excellence in patient care and service delivery.

title: Referrals Out Administrator
description: Referrals Out Administrators are an integral part of the Outpatients team, processing the onward referrals for patients who have been referred elsewhere for diagnostics or procedures. The key responsibilities are ensuring that referrals are sent within the expected timeframes, with all required information included, and actively monitoring the flow of information throughout the patient pathway. Please note: This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship, and the successful candidate must have existing right to work in the UK. We screen and shortlist suitable candidates as applications are received. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early and without notice if we fill the position. Therefore, we encourage early applications to avoid disappointment. Organisation, prioritisation, IT skills, and attention to detail will be crucial in this role as you will be responsible for sending urgent and routine referrals to other providers and ensuring they have all the information needed to continue the patient's care. You will need to gather all the relevant information from different areas of the patient record system, including booking forms, clinic letters, BMI and blood results, and chase up any missing information with the clinicians or patients. Full training will be given on how to use our patient record system and complete the role. JOB SUMMARY The role (and team) is an integral part of the patient pathway. You will undertake tasks essential to the smooth and effective provision of quality care, providing an efficient level of service for patients and their families. The role will work within the priorities and expectations set out by the Lead Referrals-Out Administrator. It is essential the post holder displays organisation, prioritisation, IT skills and attention to detail will be crucial in this role as you will be creating referrals on patient records to other providers. You will need to gather all the relevant information from the patient record system, submit it via email to the provider & update the patient record. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE POST Referral Processing Process outbound referrals for diagnostics and procedures in line with clinical instructions and referral pathways. Ensure all referrals are correctly triaged, recorded, and actioned within agreed timeframes. Liaise with clinical teams and patients to clarify referral details or gather additional information as needed. Upload or send referrals via appropriate systems (e-RS, email, secure portals). Coordination & Communication Communicate clearly and professionally with external providers (e.g., hospitals, imaging centres, specialist clinics) to confirm referral receipt and appointment arrangements. Respond to incoming queries from patients, clinicians, and third parties regarding referrals, providing updates or advice as appropriate. Monitor referral progress and follow up to ensure timely outcomes or to troubleshoot delays. Managing multiple tasks, prioritising own workload, and ensuring work is completed within target timeframes for processing routine and urgent referrals. Work closely with the wider DHC administration and clinical teams to support seamless patient journeys. Pathway Knowledge & Relationship Management Ensure knowledge and understanding of patient pathways is maintained, including referral routes and any associated criteria for trust hospitals and independent providers. Develop and maintain relationships with other providers we work closely with. Sourcing new referral pathways, ensuring referral forms are updated, and the contact address database is maintained accurately. Contribute to maintaining and updating referral protocols and standard operating procedures. Data Management & Reporting Accurately input and update referral information in clinical systems to support timely patient care. Keep thorough documentation and audit trails in line with data protection and confidentiality policies. Contribute to performance monitoring through accurate data capture and referral tracking insights. General Undertake any other reasonable duties as commensurate with the nature of this role. Maintain mandatory training compliance. WORK SETTING AND REVIEW To manage own workload efficiently and effectively on a daily basis. Maintain confidentiality at all times. Acting independently but, where necessary, referring problems to the Referrals-Out Team Leader or the appropriate consultant via the quickest route possible. CONFIDENTIALITY The post holder must maintain the confidentiality of information about patients, staff, and DHC business in accordance with the Data Protection Act 1998 and the Caldicott principles.
